title: The claim/release state machine of an agent task list, in three languages
pins: Who may hold a task, when a lease has lapsed, who may release it, and the bytes of the stored record. A task list is DURABLE state that outlives the process which wrote it, and nothing says the process reading it back is in the same language -- so the list itself is the shared surface. A one-tick disagreement about expiry hands one task to two workers. A disagreement about how claimed_by is compared lets one worker close another's work. Neither errors, and both look like ordinary operation.
scope: The claim and release paths, and the canonical record. NOT the completion tool, NOT lease extension, and NOT the store's locking primitive -- each is a separate value with its own failure mode, and this suite existing does not cover them. The generator's store uses a no-op lock deliberately: the lock has its own defects, three of which were found and fixed while this feature was built, and measuring them here would conflate two things.
construction: Each row seeds a list state DIRECTLY rather than through add(), so a row may describe a state the public API would refuse to build -- an inconsistent one, say. A corpus that can only express states the implementation is willing to create cannot test what it does when it meets one it did not. Time is frozen per row, so expiry boundaries are exact rather than raced.
findings: TypeScript is now RUN and COMPARED, and it was not the exception: 18 of the 20 rows the reference can express agree byte-for-byte, and TWO DISAGREE -- atc-0011 and atc-0012, the outcome-validation rows. A Python half was recorded alongside it and does NOT share the disagreement: Python's TaskOutcome is a runtime enum like PHP's and refuses both rows at the door, which leaves TypeScript alone of the three. Python introduces its own, on the one row PHP cannot express: atc-0017 gets THREE answers -- PHP skips a fractional lease, TypeScript refuses it, and Python ACCEPTS it and truncates 90.4 to 90, landing claimed_until on now+90, which is exactly the silent configuration change the row's title says must not happen. The disagreement is not a rename like G-20 and G-21. Both languages end up refusing, but not at the same door and not with the same consequence: PHP's TaskOutcome is an enum, so TaskOutcome::from() rejects the value AT THE CALL SITE under task_outcome_invalid and nothing is written; TypeScript's TaskOutcome is a compile-time union with no runtime existence, release() validates the worker id and not the outcome, and the string is written into the durable list as a state that is not one of the four. Nothing refuses until something READS the list back, and then every port refuses it -- unmappable_content -- because the bytes on the shared surface are junk. See G-39. atc-0017 is the other asymmetry and is not a defect: PHP SKIPS it under 0002 because claim() declares ?int and the fractional lease is rejected by the type system before any guard in the package runs, while TypeScript has no such constraint, reaches its own guard, and refuses 90.4 as a DECISION rather than a type error. Recorded as a real result rather than a skip inherited from another language. Two things were already recorded here before any port ran and both still hold: atc-0015 shows duplicate ids are guarded at add() and TOLERATED on read, so a list written by a less careful port is accepted and find() resolves the id to whichever comes first; and the reference's skip on atc-0017 has the reachable PHP path being the configuration route, which is a different value and belongs in its own row.
construction_note: The generator's seeding writes to the source's OWN key. An earlier version wrote to the bare list name, so every row read an empty list and the generator recorded 'nothing happened' for all 21 as though it were an answer -- outcome ok, pending 0, no record, entirely plausible. It now asserts the source can see the tasks it was given and exits loudly if it cannot. A generator that silently measures nothing is the defect this repository exists to catch, one level up.

ts.gap: atc-0011 and atc-0012 diverge from the reference and are recorded as `divergence` rather than skipped, because a skip would hide the finding. One cause: this port has NO RUNTIME OUTCOME GUARD on release(). The reference converts the agent-supplied string through the TaskOutcome enum at the call site and refuses `complete` and ` done` there, under task_outcome_invalid, with nothing written. Here TaskOutcome is a compile-time union, release() checks the worker id and not the outcome, and the string is written into the durable list as a state that is not one of the four -- the refusal arrives only when a reader maps the row back, as unmappable_content, for every language. The runner hands the outcome over UNVALIDATED on purpose: supplying the guard in the runner would measure the runner and record agreement the package has not earned. See G-39. Separately, atc-0017 is skipped for PHP and EXPRESSED here: a fractional lease reaches assertLease and is refused as task_lease_invalid, which is this port's own decision rather than its type system's.

py.gap: atc-0017 diverges and is recorded as a divergence rather than skipped, because a skip would hide the finding -- and it is the row where all three languages give a different answer. PHP is SKIPPED under 0002: claim() declares ?int, so 90.4 is rejected by the type system before any guard in the package runs. prism-harness-ts reaches its own guard and REFUSES it as task_lease_invalid. This port reaches _require_lease, which asks only for finite-and-positive, ACCEPTS 90.4, and then truncates in _timestamp -- granting a 90 second lease for a 90.4 second request, with claimed_until on now+90. That is the silent configuration change the row's title says must not happen, and the direction is the unsafe one: the lease expires EARLY, so the next caller may take the task while its holder still believes it holds it. Recorded rather than fixed, because refusing a non-integral lease changes shipped behaviour for a consumer passing 90.5 today and the port's own default lease is a float; that belongs in a decision across the three repositories. See G-40. The other 20 rows agree byte-for-byte, INCLUDING atc-0011 and atc-0012 where ts diverges (G-39): TaskOutcome is a runtime enum here, release() parses the outcome rather than trusting it, and the runner hands the value over unvalidated so that guard is measured rather than supplied by the runner.
py.cause_note: G-40, one row: atc-0017. The two languages that can express it disagree, and this is the one that accepts a fractional lease and truncates it. Closing it is a behaviour change in a shipped package, so it needs a decision across prism-harness, -ts and -py.
